verdictNote: Candidate 1 implements DESIGN rev 3 and the rulings faithfully. The model matches its README and R10's B1. The vectors kill 64 of 75 model mutants, and every security-relevant one in v1. The complete positive passes VPC and, on paper, every comparison VPO makes. No attack case passes wrongly. One MAJOR blocks adoption: the contract does not name the layer-test assertion that runs VPO on the complete positive (C1-1, the monitor's Q-CB-6 (b) requirement). Two MINORs add vectors (C1-2, C1-3). The NOTEs can be carried. The determinism run (C1-9) is open until the monitor rules on the build's extra read-only git forms.

findings.location: README section 10 (the complete I01 positive) and section 11; model _check_complete docstring
findings.finding: Nothing in candidate 1 runs VPO's validate_messages on the complete positive, and the contract does not name where it runs. README section 10 says only that the positive 'is built for VPO's validate_messages unchanged' and that the model re-checks the members VPO binds; _check_complete says the two validators 'are run on it outside this model'; definitions.json does not mention validate_messages. The model's main (the layer validator) passes whatever VPO would say. Under Q-CB-6 (b) the check moves into the packet's layer test, but no text requires that test to make the assertion, so the pre-check and verify could skip it silently. This review found the content sound (all 44 of VPO's comparisons hold on paper; VPC's validate_profile returns []), so the gap is the missing executable obligation, not the data.
findings.requiredChange: Add to README section 10, after the complete-positive bullet, and cite it in section 11: '**The layer test runs both validators on the complete positive.** The packet's layer test (tests/test_policy_observation_digests.py, as the packet YAML names it), which the pre-check and verify run, asserts, with no skip, expected-failure mark or import guard: (1) validate_messages(complete.binding, complete.request, complete.observation, complete.profile, CS, complete.now, complete.previous) == [], with validate_messages imported from scripts/validate_policy_observation.py and CS read from architecture/policy-observation-inputs/channel.schema.json; (2) validate_profile(complete.profile, PPS) == [], with validate_profile imported from scripts/validate_proxy_contract.py and PPS read from architecture/proxy-contract-inputs/profile.schema.json; (3) each returns its refusal when one preexisting reference's observedDigest in complete.profile is changed. The model does not import VPO; these assertions are the only executable check that the complete positive fits the I01 wire, and a layer run that does not execute them fails.' Change _check_complete's docstring to name that layer test.

findings.location: vectors G-01..G-20; README 3.3 item 2 ('and never after it'); Q-CB-9
findings.finding: The rule that the monotonic age is never negative has no vector: the mutant that drops '0 <=' from the monotonic age survives all 290 checks, although Q-CB-9 states 'a negative monotonic age refuses'. The data-level form of D3-1's hazard (a newer, advanced schedule paired with an older completed set) is caught only incidentally: the 'newest set entry' mutant dies at G-16 because G-16's incomplete set lies in the future, which is the negative-age rule again. G-09/G-10 carry no newer entry. The wall age still bounds both cases, so no security outcome changes today, but the monotonic rules are unpinned for the port.
findings.requiredChange: Add two gate vectors (both probed in WORK; the model refuses both): (a) answer.monotonicMs = latest scheduledMonotonicMs - 1 with a wall age of 30 s: all three gated values 'capture set too old'; (b) a later incomplete set entry scheduled 60 s after the latest completed set, answered 100 s after the completed set's start (40 s after the incomplete entry's): all three 'capture set too old'.

findings.location: README 4.6 ('A row without exactly those refuses'); model _broker_row; vectors MB-05, MB-06
findings.finding: The BROKER row's exactness is only partly pinned. Three mutants survive: extra members admitted, only the 14 document members required, cgroup members not checked. MB-05 deletes a document member and MB-06 replaces the whole row, so a port that checks only the document's members passes the replay. No security outcome changes, since hostPreflightDigest binds the whole record, but the README's rule is unpinned.
findings.requiredChange: Add vectors that refuse 'mutationBroker: broker row incomplete' for: roles.BROKER.rlimitCore deleted, roles.BROKER.cgroup.pidsMax deleted, and an extra member added to roles.BROKER.

findings.finding: Four sub-rules of v1's NetworkPolicy form have no vector. Their mutants survive: a peer with ipBlock plus a selector, a non-integer endPort, a rule with an extra member, a port with an extra member. In v1 the default-deny binding makes any added rule change the digest. Kubernetes validation (general knowledge, not a pinned source) also forbids ipBlock beside a selector and prunes unknown members. The first sub-rule is R1-A's core statement ('ipBlock and no other member').
findings.requiredChange: Add at least a vector for a peer {ipBlock, podSelector} refusing 'networkPolicy: selector form outside v1'; the three others are optional.

findings.location: README 4.5 ('in B1's order'); definitions b1Refusals.order; model _rbac bindings.sort
findings.finding: B1's binding order is not pinned: removing the sort survives. The model builds ClusterRoleBindings before RoleBindings either way, so the order matters only among ClusterRoleBindings by name, or RoleBindings by namespace and name, when two of them refuse differently. It affects which refusal text is reported, not whether the snapshot refuses. B1 itself matches the model (rbac.rs:251-353 read in full).
findings.requiredChange: Optional: a vector with two ClusterRoleBindings listed out of name order, 'z' with an unknown subject kind before 'a' with a dangling roleRef, expecting 'rbac: role does not exist'.

findings.location: definitions refusalTexts and the rbac and rbacClosureDigest refusal lists
findings.finding: Q-CB-12 holds: all 27 unvectored texts are raised only in document_bound (model lines 194, 202, 203, 205), reached from its five call sites (271, 507, 579, 639, 641) with the key as a prefix only. Four of them can never occur, though: 'rbac: float refused', 'rbac: integer out of range', 'rbacClosureDigest: float refused' and 'rbacClosureDigest: integer out of range'. Both RBAC documents hold only B1-validated strings and booleans. Probed: a float in any RBAC input slot gives B1's malformed texts, or is dropped as an unread member.
findings.requiredChange: Drop those four from refusalTexts, or mark them unreachable, so that a port does not look for a way to produce them.

findings.location: README 3.3 item 3, 'The port', and section 11; definitions captureGate.dataShape
findings.finding: The wall age compares answer.wallMs with set_started_ms, which is milliseconds (R10:obs/capture.rs:1250, compared with valid_from x 1000 at :1251). R10's I01 service is handed only the wire's wall second (R10:obs/client.rs:274-275). A port that scales that second by 1000 sees a negative wall age for answers in the same second as a set's start, a spurious refusal (availability only). A port that truncates the start to seconds loosens the wall check by under 1 s.
findings.requiredChange: State in README 3.3 'The port' that the answer's wall time is a millisecond reading of the same wall clock as set_started_ms, handed to the I01 service with the view.

findings.finding: The contract README is vendored BYTE_IDENTICAL into R10 by edge v10, yet it carries 'CONTRACT_CANDIDATE_1_AWAITING_INDEPENDENT_REVIEW'. README-v10 uses a different token, 'CONTRACT_CANDIDATE_ROUND1_AWAITING_INDEPENDENT_REVIEW'. Any status change at adoption changes the README's bytes and the edge row's sha256.
findings.requiredChange: Give both files their final status text, or none (status.json holds adoption), in the candidate that is adopted, and derive edge v10's row from those bytes.

findings.finding: build_contract.py reads its inputs with git show, but it also runs these read-only git forms: rev-parse PIN; log -1 --format=%H PIN -- <file> (the LAST_CHANGE files and the frozen models); ls-tree PIN -- architecture/proxy-contract-inputs/vectors.json (one file entry); diff --name-only 26a8affb PIN -- <input files>; and cat-file -e PIN:<path> (the six new paths). All set GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0. None lists a directory, and none names VPO or an excluded path. Because the launch prompt allowed running it only if it uses git show alone, this review did not run it, and the determinism check (brief check 6) is open.
findings.requiredChange: Before round 2, the monitor either allows these five read-only forms for the reviewer's two determinism runs, or the builder states them in the brief and report. The determinism run is then done in round 2.

findings.location: BUILD_REPORT_C1 section 8 rows R1-7 and R2-38
findings.finding: Two attack-case mappings are by analogy. R1-7 (an impersonation or bind/escalate grant) maps to RC-03, which is a create-resourcequotas grant on the same I06 closure path. R2-38 (non-resource rules duplicated or reordered) maps to RB-11, which uses resource rules. Both outcomes hold. I06's frozen closure check refuses grants outside the closure. On paper, from lines 36-53. A normal non-isolated run of scripts/policy_observation_digests.py puts scripts/ on sys.path, so the first form succeeds. A repository-root import as scripts.policy_observation_digests (TPO's pattern, 'from scripts.X import') puts the root on sys.path, so the second form succeeds. The fallback is reached only when neither is importable, as under python3 -I with a path argument (the self-check). There it inserts the model's own directory, which in a checkout is the same scripts/, so no other VPC can load. The one side effect is that the insertion persists for the process. An ImportError inside VPC's own imports passes through the fallback and is raised again.
